articles.title: Como secar roupa rápido no frio e na chuva: veja dicas práticas | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialistas explicam como o vento, a umidade e até o tipo de varal influenciam na secagem das roupas e o que realmente funciona em espaços pequenos.
articles.summary: Aprenda como secar roupa rápido no frio e em apartamentos usando técnicas de ventilação, desumidificadores e a disposição correta das peças no varal.
articles.body:
Em dias frios, chuvosos ou úmidos, secar a roupa lavada parece levar uma eternidade. Para quem mora em apartamento, onde muitas vezes não há varal externo nem espaço para a ventilação natural fazer seu trabalho, esse problema é ainda pior.

Mas a boa notícia é que, com algumas estratégias práticas, é possível acelerar a secagem das roupas, mesmo em dias sem sol.

O g1 conversou com especialistas e reuniu orientações para diferentes situações: desde truques que melhoram a circulação de ar no varal de chão até orientações para quem tem um quintal aberto .

Além disso, o Guia de Compras também traz dicas sobre as vantagens e limitações da máquina lava e seca, para quem está pensando em adquirir um modelo. Leia abaixo.

Dois fatores principais influenciam a velocidade de secagem das roupas no varal: a umidade do ar e a ventilação do ambiente.

O frio ou o calor também interferem, mas isso pode ser compensado se o dia estiver com baixa umidade e boa ventilação.

“Busque lavar as roupas em dias menos nublados, com mais vento, com mais sol , mesmo no frio”, afirma Brenno Henrique, professor do departamento de engenharia têxtil da UFSC.

Peça de roupa foi deixada na relva e congelou com frio na Serra de SC — Foto: Mycchel Legnaghi/São Joaquim Online

🌬️ Se você tem varal externo, faça isso:

Evite estender roupa em dias de chuva, mesmo se seu varal estiver em uma área coberta.

Lave poucas roupas por vez. “Com o varal mais vazio, o ar circula mais facilmente e as roupas secam mais rapidamente”, explica a Omo Lavanderia.

Evite dobrar as roupas ao pendurá-las. “Roupas dobradas demoram para secar. Use cabides em vez de pregadores e deixe um espaço mínimo de um palmo fechado entre eles”, diz a Omo.

🏠 Se você tiver varal interno ou de chão, faça isso:

Se sua casa não tem ventilação, use um ventilador . “Coloque o ventilador voltado para as roupas e deixe ligado por um tempo, de forma que o ar circule bem entre as peças”, sugere Henrique.

No frio, use um desumidificador. “Quando está frio e úmido, e o apartamento é muito pequeno para ventilação, o desumidificador retira a umidade do ar e ajuda a secar as roupas”, explica o professor.

⚠️ Atenção: por segurança, nunca tente secar as roupas com o ferro de passar, micro-ondas ou pendurando atrás da geladeira . O uso inadequado dos aparelhos pode causar acidentes.

Além disso, jamais use lareiras ou calor do fogo para secar roupas . “O algodão é muito inflamável, então pega fogo muito fácil”, alerta Henrique.

🤔 Vale a pena investir em uma lava e seca?

Outra opção, principalmente para quem mora em apartamento pequeno, é comprar uma máquina lava e seca, que já entrega suas roupas (quase) secas sem a necessidade do varal. Mas elas têm vantagens e desvantagens.

“A vantagem é que são muito práticas, rápidas e eficientes em secar a roupa em qualquer condição de tempo ”, diz Brenno Henrique. “São muito indicadas para toalhas, lençóis, tapetes e toalha de mesa. Esses tecidos que são mais grossos e mais resistentes – e mais difíceis de secar também”.

“Porém, com tecidos mais delicados, a máquina pode esticar e deformar as peças, encolher . Normalmente, a maioria das peças de malha, lã e seda pode deformar”, avisa Henrique.

Também é bom lembrar que esses eletrodomésticos têm capacidades diferentes para lavagem e secagem – ou seja, lavam uma quantidade maior de roupas do que secam de uma vez só.

Outra questão é que as roupas nem sempre saem completamente secas. Ainda assim, é uma grande ajuda para quem tem dificuldade de secar de outras formas.

Ele também é um aparelho caro; em setembr, os modelos de lava e seca vendidos na internet começavam em R$ 3.000. Leia o Guia de Compras sobre as máquinas para entender mais sobre os pontos positivos e negativos desse eletrodoméstico.

articles.title: Woman was high when she plowed her SUV into a Metro bus, killing 2, prosecutors say
articles.summary: The woman accused of being behind the wheel of an SUV in a deadly crash involving a Metro bus was charged with two counts of murder Thursday, as families and...
articles.body:
The 36-year-old woman charged with murder in a violent, high-speed crash that killed two people in Chatsworth on Tuesday was under the influence of drugs and had narcotics in the car when she drove the wrong way on city streets and broadsided a Metro bus, prosecutors said.

The Los Angeles County district attorney's office on Thursday charged Bailee Lynn Rios with reckless driving, driving under the influence and two counts of second-degree murder in the deaths of 46-year-old Daniel Castillo and 31-year-old Gage Weida, who was ejected from the bus during the crash.

"The tragedy of the Rios car crash was entirely preventable," Dist. Atty. Nathan Hochman said during a news conference on Thursday.

Rios was not charged in connection with the helicopter crash that claimed the lives of a pilot, an NBC4 reporter and a bystander. The helicopter had been hovering a few blocks from the traffic collision, providing a live feed for television news, when it appeared to suddenly lose power and crash.

Rios was scheduled to be arraigned Thursday in San Fernando court, but was not taken from the jail to the courthouse because of a medical event. She is now expected to appear in court on Friday, according to officials.

If convicted, she faces a maximum sentence of life in prison, Hochman said.

Video footage of the crash show Rios' 2004 Ford Expedition speeding on the wrong side of the road on De Soto Avenue, barreling through a red light at the intersection where the avenue meets Nordhoff Street, at roughly 5 p.m. The SUV narrowly avoids a car in the intersection before plowing directly into the side of the Metro Line 166 bus.

Rush hour traffic was moving slowly when Rios' Expedition entered one of the busiest junctions in the San Fernando Valley, but the SUV did not appear to brake before it T-boned the bus, witnesses said.

The impact was so powerful that the front end of the SUV nearly disappeared into the bus' frame. Castillo and Weida died at the scene. One passenger, who suffered severe injuries, and five others with non-life-threatening injures were taken to hospitals.

Rios mother, Cindy Rios, declined to comment to The Times when reached by phone on Thursday. But she told the Associated Press this week that she was sorry for the families involved.

"The fact that my daughter was involved and was the cause of it is just extremely disturbing," she told the outlet. "My daughter's alive. People lost their lives."

Investigators gathered video from a matrix of security cameras that surround the busy intersection to support their contention that Rios' actions amounted to murder with implied malice, according to law enforcement sources.

Authorities are also reviewing the SUV's event data recorder to determine Rios' speed, braking and acceleration in the seconds before the deadly crash.

That data proved key in prosecutors securing a double murder conviction in 2024 against Rebecca Grossman . In that case, prosecutors said Grossman was impaired by alcohol and Valium when she recklessly sped her Mercedes through a residential neighborhood, chasing her ex-Dodger boyfriend before killing two young boys in a crosswalk .

Prosecutors can prove murder charges based on someone's intent to kill or through a defendant's conscious disregard for human life, known as implied malice, legal experts told The Times.

"If you voluntarily behave in a manner that is so obviously and inherently dangerous to human life...a jury could say you're acting with a wanton and malignant heart," said Matt Murphy, a former Orange County homicide prosecutor.

Dmitry Gorin, a former prosecutor, said in this case authorities would be able to prove implied malice from Rios' driving.

"Here, the alleged wrong-way driving, high speed, running a red light, and near collision before striking the bus could be used to show she knew her conduct was dangerous to human life and continued anyway," he said.

The conduct and the resulting deaths would be a "very compelling theory for a jury to find her guilty of murder," Gorin said.

Court records and interviews paint a picture of Rios as a woman who had long been dogged by drug addiction.

Rios' friend Lanise Ward told The Times in an interview that Rios was sober when the two met for lunch about a month ago. She had been going to Narcotics Anonymous meetings and had been clean for the longest stretch since she began using drugs as a teen, Ward said.

"I really thought this time she was going to do it," Ward said. "She had been clean for a year and a half already."

In Simi Valley, where Rios spent much of her life, she had been arrested more than a dozen times by local police mostly on suspicion of drug-related offenses, authorities told The Times. However, the majority of the arrests do not appear to have resulted in criminal charges, Ventura County court records show.

Ward said Rios told her she began using drugs at 14 and struggled with an addiction to heroin. Rios had been to rehab several times, but couldn't seem to kick the habit long term until recently, Ward said.

Ward said if Rios relapsed she likely felt deep shame about it.

"I think she was disappointed in herself for getting high again, and I think she was trying to just end it all," Ward said.

In 2016, Rios was charged with possessing Xanax without a prescription and methamphetamine, both misdemeanors. The court dismissed the Xanax possession count and Rios pleaded guilty to the meth possession charge. She was placed on probation, ordered to submit to random drug tests and was referred to a drug treatment program, according to court records.

Less than a year later, she was accused of violating the terms of her probation, but was given a second chance and ordered to re-enroll in a drug treatment program. In 2018, court records show, she again violated probation and was mandated to a treatment program.

In 2019, she violated probation a third time and was granted conditional revocable release meaning if she got in trouble again she could face jail time, according to court records.

In 2022, Rios was back in court facing misdemeanor charges for being under the influence of a drugs, possession of heroin and Alprazolam, a benzodiazepine commonly prescribed to treat anxiety or panic disorders, and possession of an injection device.

She was also charged with an infraction for driving with a suspended or revoked license. The circumstances around her license suspension were not immediately available. Court records note that it was the result of an accident, but provided no additional detail.

A judge granted her diversion for four months, ordering that she enroll in a Narcotics Anonymous program, which she successfully completed, records show. She ultimately pleaded no contest to driving with a suspended license.

While Rios has no history of receiving a warning from a judge, called a Watson advisement—commonly issued after a driving under the influence conviction—L.A. County prosecutors have used warnings given by officers or others during traffic stops or other incidents to prove defendants showed a disregard for human life.

During the Grossman trial, a California Highway Patrol officer testified that he stopped her for speeding and warned that her that driving above the speed limit could have fatal consequences.

While prosecutors don't need a Watson advisement to prove second-degree murder it "is a very powerful piece of evidence if they have it," said defense attorney, Glen Jonas.

"Where there is no record of a court advisement, prosecutors scour prior reports and body cam footage to prove the defendant received a prior warning that her illegal conduct is in inherently dangerous to human life," Jonas said.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: His wife encouraged his ‘American Idol’ dream. Now he stands trial for her murder
articles.summary: Flynn will stand trial for his wife’s murder, as investigators allege the former music pastor fatally shot her and staged the crime scene.
articles.body:
About 13 years ago, "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn gushed about his wife Ashley, who he said encouraged him to audition for the 12th season of ABC's singing competition.

"I love my wife more than anything," he said in an interview during his brief stint on the show . "She's very, very pretty, just – woof, I love her."

Now, Flynn stands trial for her murder, as investigators allege the former music pastor fatally shot his wife of almost 16 years and staged the crime scene to make it appear she was killed by an intruder.

Flynn, 40, was arrested in February, days after he frantically called 911 to report someone broke into their Tipp City, Ohio, home and killed his wife – a beloved middle school volleyball coach – while he was in their daughters' bedroom.

"We're looking forward to trying the case," his defense attorney, Patrick Mulligan, told CNN Tuesday. "We've been waiting for this."

Flynn has pleaded not guilty to charges of aggravated murder, murder, felonious assault, and tampering with evidence.

The murder trial, which is slated to last about two weeks, started with jury selection on Thursday. Sixteen panelists – four of whom have been designated alternates – were seated, according to CNN affiliate WHIO . Opening statements are expected Friday morning.

During the proceedings, the jurors are expected to visit the family's home to view the crime scene and hear testimony from several of Ashley's family members – including the couple's preteen daughters, who are crucial to their father's presumed alibi.

Prosecutors have provided scant details about the investigation and have not yet offered a purported motive for the killing or described the alleged "cover up" – key components jurors will likely consider during their deliberations.

"It will become apparent what the status of the evidence is as things go on," Mulligan told CNN, adding he didn't believe the prosecution would be able to prove the charges beyond a reasonable doubt. He previously suggested authorities had made a "rush to judgment" in arresting his client.

"When the government runs out of leads or can't develop leads and looks at a surviving spouse in cases such as these, the chance of a wrongful conviction increases," the defense attorney said in a statement to The Associated Press shortly after Flynn's arrest in February.

If the panel convicts Flynn of the most serious charge, he could be sentenced to life in prison without parole .

Weeks before the trial's start, Judge Jeannine Pratt denied a defense motion to change the venue of the trial and a motion from prosecutors to sequester the jury, with both parties arguing the high public interest in the case could jeopardize the impartiality of the panel.

The court will impose additional measures to ensure jurors are impartial, Pratt wrote in her ruling, and may reconsider the parties' requests if any issues arise while seating the jury.

In the early morning hours of February 16, Ashley was shot and killed inside the suburban home she shared with her husband and their two daughters.

Caleb Flynn told investigators he was sleeping in the living room that night because he had a bad cough, according to a conversation captured on police body-worn cameras. He woke up when he heard one of their dogs moving, he said, and assumed one of the children had gotten out of bed.

"I went in their room, and I laid down with them for – I don't even know how long, and that's when I heard it," Flynn told the officers, saying he "froze" when he heard a gunshot.

"When I finally got up, the door leading to the garage was open, but I didn't see anybody," he said.

In a 911 call around 2:30 a.m., Flynn reported an intruder had broken into the house and shot his wife.

"My wife, she's got two shots to her head. There's blood everywhere," he said breathlessly. "Oh my God, oh my God, oh my God."

Footage from police body cameras showed first responders rushing into the family's home shortly after and clearing the house with their guns drawn.

"We have a lady with a gunshot wound to the head in her bed," one officer said. "We got gun casings on the floor. The husband's here and the kids are here."

While searching through the garage, police noted a door leading outside was open, as was the center console in a parked truck. Flynn told investigators he had a few guns in the house, including a handgun he stored in his truck, according to the footage.

As officers secured the scene over the next hour, police bodycam footage captured Flynn sobbing, calling loved ones and appearing to vomit. When Ashley's mother arrived at the home, he fell to his knees, wailing, before they embraced on the front lawn.

"The girls don't know, the girls are sleeping," Flynn said as he hugged her. "I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do."

"I don't know what to do either," the grandmother said through tears. "I'm just – I'm in shock."

Police led astray by 'staging of the crime scene,' they say

That night, Flynn agreed to go to the police station to provide a statement about the incident, the bodycam footage shows. "You'll be riding up front with me," an officer told him as he pointed to a nearby car.

Three days later, Flynn was handcuffed in the back of a police vehicle on his way to the Miami County Jail, where he's been held since his arrest. His bond was set at $3.5 million.

Initial charging documents said officers were at first "lead estray (sic) by the staging of the crime scene," though authorities have not provided details about the alleged cover-up.

"As a result of the investigation, probable cause existed to charge Caleb Flynn with the murder of his wife," Tipp City police said in a news release announcing his arrest. "Due to the ongoing nature of this case, specific investigative details will not be released at this time."

Ashley's family believes the arrest was made "carefully and not without serious consideration," according to a statement shared with CNN affiliate WKEF .

"After speaking with both local police and federal authorities, we trust the proper steps were taken and the process is being handled appropriately," they wrote. "We kindly ask for privacy as we work through this complex situation."

Friends and family mourn a 'pillar' of the community

In the aftermath of her shocking death, the suburban community of Tipp City – just north of Dayton – came together to mourn Ashley, a beloved substitute teacher and volleyball coach.

Ribbons and Bible verses adorned the downtown streets in her memory, and local restaurants donated some of their proceeds to her family, according to CNN affiliate WHIO .

"She was such a pillar to the community," neighbor Tia Turner told WKEF . "She was one of the first people to welcome us in the neighborhood."

About a week after her death, Ashley's friends and family commemorated what would have been her 38th birthday. Her daughters blew out candles on chocolate cupcakes, WKEF reported, and her loved ones released balloons with handwritten messages into the sky.

"We miss her in ways words can't capture. But we hold tightly to this: Ashley's life was always about pointing people to Jesus and showing them His love," her family said in a statement provided to WKEF .

"And her legacy will live on – in her daughters, in her parents, in her sister, and in the many lives she touched and influenced along the way."

articles.title: São José (SC): concurso abre 300 vagas para auxiliar de educação | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidade da Grande Florianópolis oferta salários de até R$ 4,5 mil. Inscrições vão até 16 de outubro e provas acontecem em 1° de novembro.
articles.summary: Cidade da Grande Florianópolis oferta salários de até R$ 4,5 mil. Inscrições vão até 16 de outubro e provas acontecem em 1° de novembro.
articles.body:
Sala de aula — Foto: Prefeitura de São Cristóvão

A prefeitura de São José , cidade de 301 mil habitantes na Grande Florianópolis, lançou concurso público com 300 vagas para o cargo de auxiliar de educação especial, destinado a profissionais com nível superior em pedagogia. As inscrições estão abertas e vão até às 16h do dia 16 de outubro (confira o edital completo abaixo) .

A seleção será através de prova objetiva marcada para 1° de novembro. As vagas estão divididas em duas áreas e o candidato deverá escolher uma única opção no ato da inscrição.

100 vagas para atuação na educação infantil: carga horária de 30 horas semanais e salário inicial de R$ 3.436,41

200 vagas para atuação no ensino fundamental: carga horária de 40 horas semanais e salário inicial de R$ 4.581,88

As inscrições devem ser feitas exclusivamente pela internet, no site da banca organizadora, a Fundação de Estudos e Pesquisas Socioeconômicos (Fepese). A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 120.

Conforme o edital, o auxiliar de educação especial atua no auxílio às crianças/estudantes com deficiência e transtorno do espectro autista em atividades de alimentação, higiene e locomoção.

O profissional deve apoiar nas atividades diárias, mediação pedagógica, estímulo à autonomia, inclusão social e construir uma cultura escolar que valorize a diversidade e promova o respeito às diferenças.

articles.title: Homem é condenado por perseguir mulher e terá de pagar R$ 5 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima relatou que foi perseguida após dizer que não queria mais contato; TJMG manteve a condenação por danos morais.
articles.summary: Vítima relatou que foi perseguida após dizer que não queria mais contato; TJMG manteve a condenação por danos morais.
articles.body:
Um homem foi condenado pelo Tribunal de Justiça de Minas Gerais (TJMG) por perseguir a ex-companheira em Juiz de Fora . Ele deverá pagar R$ 5 mil por danos morais à vítima .

O caso começou após o homem entrar na Justiça contra a mulher, alegando que ela havia feito uma falsa denúncia de perseguição e pedido uma medida protetiva contra ele. Ele pediu R$ 50 mil por danos morais e mais R$ 600 referentes a gastos com advogado.

Segundo o homem, os dois mantiveram contato frequente e consentido em 2021, mas, após o fim da relação, ele teria sido acusado injustamente de perseguição e violência psicológica. Ele afirmou ainda que nunca a ameaçou e que as passagens frequentes por locais próximos à casa dela aconteciam porque, por recomendação médica, precisava fazer caminhadas.

Em defesa, a mulher manteve as acusações e apresentou detalhes das mensagens trocadas entre os dois. Ela também pediu que o homem fosse condenado a indenizá-la.

Segundo o relato apresentado à Justiça, depois que ela informou que não queria mais contato, o homem passou a persegui-la . Disse ainda que ele criou perfis falsos em redes sociais, monitorou sua rotina, entrou em contato com familiares e passou a caminhar próximo a residência dela.

A vítima também relatou que o homem teria agredido um amigo dela com um canivete. Para ela, o episódio aumentou o medo e reforçou a necessidade de medidas protetivas.

A Justiça de Juiz de Fora rejeitou o pedido feito pelo homem e acolheu a solicitação da mulher. Na avaliação do juízo, não houve falsa denúncia, mas o exercício do direito de buscar proteção policial e judicial diante de uma situação de risco.

A sentença determinou que o homem pagasse R$ 5 mil por danos morais. O entendimento foi de que a insistência nos contatos, a criação de perfis falsos e o episódio de violência contra terceiros afetaram a tranquilidade e a integridade da vítima.

O recurso foi analisado pela 11ª Câmara Cível do TJMG. O relator, desembargador Rui de Almeida Magalhães, votou a favor da condenação. O entendimento foi acompanhado pelos desembargadores Marcelo Pereira da Silva e Mônica Libânio Rocha Bretas.

O relator afirmou que as provas apresentadas no processo demonstraram a violação à privacidade e à integridade psicológica da mulher.

Para o magistrado, registrar boletins de ocorrência e solicitar medidas protetivas não configura ato ilícito quando existem elementos concretos que indiquem ameaça ou perseguição.

Na decisão, o desembargador destacou que o momento determinante foi quando a mulher manifestou expressamente que não queria mais manter contato. A partir daí, segundo o voto, a insistência, a criação de perfis falsos para contornar bloqueios e a aproximação de locais frequentados por ela deixaram de ser uma simples inconveniência e passaram a configurar uma conduta ilícita.

Com a decisão, foi mantida a indenização de R$ 5 mil por danos morais à vítima.

articles.title: Geraldo Carvalho defende reestatização da Agespisa no Piauí | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato do PSTU cita a Agespisa como alvo de "desprivatização" do Piauí. Até o sábado (19), o PITV 1 exibe entrevistas com os candidatos ao Governo do Piauí que registraram menos de 5% das intenções de voto na pesquisa Datafolha.
articles.summary: Geraldo Carvalho (PSTU) defende concursos públicos e o fim da terceirização no Piauí em entrevista sobre suas propostas de governo ao PITV 1.
articles.body:
O candidato ao Governo do Piauí, Geraldo Carvalho (PTSU), defendeu nesta sexta-feira (18), em entrevista ao PITV 1 , a reestatização de empresas privatizadas, como a Companhia Energética do Piauí (Cepisa) e Águas e Esgotos do Piauí (Agespisa).

Além disso, o candidato propõe a realização de concurso para contratação de funcionários públicos, como maneira de substituição de empresas e servidores terceirizados no funcionamento público.

"Estamos defendendo a necessidade de desprivatizar o estado. Isso significa reestatizar as empresas estatais que foram privatizadas, como a nossa antiga Cepisa, hoje a Agespisa, mas outras estatais que foram também privatizadas. No transporte, nós estamos defendendo a criação de uma empresa pública de transporte coletivo para que fosse dar o transporte, devolver o transporte para a população. [...] Precisamos acabar com a terceirização, fazer concurso para a contratação efetiva, e construir um estado sob o controle da população e tirar o controle das grandes empresas", disse o candidato Geraldo Carvalho.

Entre quarta-feira (16) e sábado (19), o PITV 1 exibe entrevistas com os candidatos ao Governo do Piauí que registraram menos de 5% das intenções de voto na pesquisa Datafolha. Cada entrevista tem duração de, no máximo, dois minutos.

Candidata ao Governo do Piauí, Geraldo Carvalho (PSTU), à Rede Clube — Foto: Rede Clube

Na segunda-feira (14) e na terça-feira (15), o PITV 1 entrevistou os dois candidatos ao Governo do Piauí mais bem colocados na pesquisa Datafolha divulgada em 22 de agosto. Rafael Fonteles (PT) aparece na liderança, com 55% das intenções de voto, seguido por Joel Rodrigues (PP), com 25%.

articles.title: Câmara de Itanhaém, SP, abre inscrições para concurso público | G1
articles.standfirst: Há oportunidades para candidatos com formação de níveis médio, técnico e superior.
articles.summary: Há oportunidades para candidatos com formação de níveis médio, técnico e superior. Salários variam de R$ 4,1 mil a R$ 7 mil.
articles.body:
Câmara Municipal de Itanhaém, SP — Foto: Prefeitura de Itanhaém/Divulgação

A Câmara Municipal de Itanhaém , no litoral de São Paulo, está com inscrições abertas para um concurso público com salários que variam de R$ 4,1 mil a R$ 7 mil. Há oportunidades para candidatos com formação de níveis médio, técnico e superior.

Ao todo, são 27 vagas distribuídas em 11 cargos, sendo que dois deles são destinados a candidatos com ensino médio completo, três exigem ensino técnico e seis necessitam de formação superior.

As inscrições devem ser realizadas no site oficial da Fundação Vunesp até às 23h59 do dia 19 de outubro de 2026. As taxas de inscrição custam R$ 80 para os cargos de nível médio/técnico e R$ 115 para os cargos de nível superior.

O concurso também prevê três vagas reservadas para pessoas com deficiência (PCD). A previsão é que a prova objetiva ocorra no dia 6 de dezembro de 2026, nos períodos da manhã e da tarde.

articles.title: Dia Nacional da TV: O projeto de Bauru que moldou afiliadas Globo | G1
articles.standfirst: Rede Globo Oeste Paulista estreou em 24 de outubro de 1984, idealizada por Boni, e deu origem ao modelo replicado pela emissora em todo o país.
articles.summary: No Dia Nacional da TV, conheça a história do projeto de Boni em Bauru que criou o modelo de afiliadas da Globo hoje replicado em todo o Brasil.
articles.body:
Em 24 de outubro de 1984, Bauru (SP) se tornava mais uma vez pioneira na televisão brasileira. A estreia da Rede Globo Oeste Paulista marcou a criação do primeiro projeto de interiorização da TV Globo , que deu origem ao sistema de afiliadas usado pela emissora até hoje em todo o país.

Nesta sexta-feira (18) é celebrado o Dia Nacional da Televisão , em referência à primeira transmissão de TV no Brasil, feita pela TV Tupi em 18 de setembro de 1950. Hoje a TV Globo é a maior emissora do país, e nesta data o g1 conta como Bauru teve papel decisivo na história da rede.

Fachada Rede Globo Oeste Paulista em Bauru — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

O projeto, idealizado por José Bonifácio de Oliveira Sobrinho, o Boni, nasceu com a missão de aproximar o jornalismo do interior paulista e acabou se tornando a matriz estrutural do sistema de afiliadas da Globo.

A novidade ocupou a concessão histórica do Canal 2, que entrou no ar pela primeira vez em 1º de agosto de 1960 como TV Bauru, fruto do sonho do empresário João Simonetti de criar o primeiro canal fora de uma capital na América Latina.

Por conta dos altos custos de manutenção, a emissora foi vendida ainda no início para a Organização Victor Costa (OVC). Em 1965, quando a OVC foi incorporada ao Grupo Globo, passou a operar como retransmissora com bloco local.

No final de 1973, a programação local foi interrompida por um hiato de sete anos, período em que uma única equipe cobria todo o interior e enviava fitas gravadas para São Paulo.

Equipe de reportagem da Rede Globo Oeste Paulista — Foto: Arquivo/TV TEM

Até que, em 1984, com a estreia da Rede Globo Oeste Paulista, a emissora passou a integrar oficialmente a Central Globo de Jornalismo (CGJ) e se consolidou como produtora de conteúdo jornalístico regional. A ideia era aproximar o jornalismo da Globo das cidades do interior, um conceito pioneiro que moldou o modelo de afiliadas em todo o Brasil.

Com central de edição em Bauru e sucursais em Marília , Presidente Prudente , Araçatuba e São José do Rio Preto , a implantação foi liderada pela jornalista Neusa Rocha e exigiu a importação de profissionais de outros estados devido à falta de editores locais.

"A gente começou a montar toda a parte de edição em Bauru. Foi bem complicado, porque não tinha editor na cidade, então a gente tinha que importar gente do Paraná, de São Paulo, do Mato Grosso...", recorda Neusa.

Amauri Soares e o jornalista Celso Pelosi, na Rede Globo Oeste Paulista — Foto: Arquivo/TV TEM

Foi nesse ambiente de inovação comunitária que surgiram nomes como o bauruense Amauri Soares, atual Diretor dos Estúdios Globo, que destaca até hoje o aprendizado dessa fase:

"Você faz televisão para as pessoas que você encontra no dia a dia. Na fila do banco, no supermercado. Essa televisão próxima, responsável, que se vê como parte da comunidade, é a televisão que eu aprendi a fazer e faço até hoje" , afirma Amauri.

Gilberto Barros, que entrou na emissora ainda na década de 1980, foi o primeiro apresentador fixo do jornal local após anos sem produção regional. Ele participou da estreia dos blocos regionais do SPTV e acompanhou o nascimento das novas sedes do projeto.

"O teleprompter era uma manivela. A gente inventou com bobina de Telex", conta Gilberto.

Gilberto Barros apresentando o SPTV na Rede Globo Oeste Paulista em Bauru (SP) — Foto: Arquivo/TV TEM

Além disso, ele fazia reportagens fora do estúdio, e as câmeras usadas em externas muitas vezes eram as mesmas da estrutura interna.

"Fiz a reportagem, corri para Bauru, editamos a matéria, fui guiando a Veraneio, cortando Bauru. Entrei correndo, jogava a fita na mão do supervisor e sentava no estúdio: 'Boa noite'", lembra.

Fachada da Rádio PRG-8 em Bauru (SP) — Foto: Arquivo/TV TEM

Em 1º de agosto de 1960, quando a TV Bauru, criada pelo empresário João Simonetti, entrou no ar pela primeira vez, o desafio não era apenas transmitir, mas inventar a televisão. Sem videotape, que permite a reprodução de conteúdos gravados, e sem modelo a seguir, o que se via no ar era feito ao vivo, no improviso, com criatividade e coragem.

"Era programa ao vivo. Se errou, está errado. A programação começava às 14h e ia até 0h", lembrou Paulo Simonetti, neto de João Simonetti, criador da TV Bauru.

Eram justamente as transmissões 100% ao vivo que atraíam a curiosidade da população de Bauru. Abel Fernando, um dos primeiros apresentadores da emissora e também seu diretor artístico, foi uma das figuras mais marcantes dessa fase.

A concessão veio com a condição de que a cidade tivesse, no mínimo, mil televisores vendidos e instalados. A família firmou uma parceria com a empresa Rebratel, que fabricava os aparelhos. Abel se recorda de uma das primeiras ações da emissora para conseguir vender televisores, a qual parou um dos principais centros comerciais da cidade:

"Trânsito impedido! Por quê? Porque ia ser feita uma demonstração para o povo que não conhecia a televisão. Aquele povo todo que frequentava as vitrines da Batista de Carvalho se concentrou ali para ver o que era a televisão. 'Ó, o senhor vai aparecer ali naquele aparelho, está vendo? Não assusta, não…'. Quando acenderam o painel de mil velas, o homem arregalou os olhos. Assim que viu sua imagem se mexendo no aparelho, mexeu no chapéu, viu o chapéu se mexer na tela e saiu correndo, assustado, sob gargalhadas do povo."

Teleteatros encenados ao vivo faziam parte da programação da TV Bauru - Canal 2 — Foto: Arquivo/TV TEM

Os primeiros formatos misturavam jornalismo, entretenimento e cultura. O teleteatro, os programas musicais e até apresentações de bandas ao vivo faziam parte da grade diária.

O estúdio improvisado surgiu no mesmo espaço onde funcionava a Rádio Bauru Clube (PRG-8), no bairro Bela Vista. O antigo auditório foi transformado em estúdio, com câmeras limitadas e soluções criativas para luz e cenário.

"Lá na Bela Vista, onde era a rádio, tinha o auditório. Então, nós acabamos com o auditório e passou a ser a TV ali mesmo", lembra Paulo Simonetti.

Grandes nomes da música brasileira lembram dos estúdios da TV Bauru. Ao lado de bandas locais, esses artistas tinham presença marcante na programação. O cantor e compositor Moacyr Franco foi um deles e se apresentou na emissora na década de 1970.

Moacyr Franco se apresentou na TV Bauru - Canal 2 — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal

"O estúdio era bem rudimentar, bem 'simplinho', com aqueles panelões de luz. Então, o estúdio era um forno, era quente, uma barbaridade. A gente suava, ensopava, mas aquela televisão foi muito emblemática. Não tinha gravação, era 'na marra', né?", lembrou o compositor em entrevista à TV TEM.

Em 1998, a emissora passou por uma nova reestruturação, tornando-se TV Modelo e ajustando sua área de cobertura.

Quatro anos antes, em 1994, Presidente Prudente deixou a Rede Globo Oeste Paulista. Anos antes, São José do Rio Preto e Araçatuba já tinham saído da cobertura de Bauru e se transformado em Globo Noroeste Paulista.

Fachada TV Modelo em Bauru — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

Com a transição para a TV Modelo , a emissora passou por uma mudança filosófica de maior aproximação com a comunidade. A televisão do interior falava com nomes e rostos conhecidos, com as histórias do bairro e da cidade.

"Foi um grande projeto. A TV virou mais comunitária. A gente falava com a Dona Maria, com o Seu José. As pautas ficaram mais locais", explica Tânia Guerra, que entrou em 1996 e viveu as fases da Globo Oeste Paulista, TV Modelo e TV TEM.

Foi nessa fase que surgiram quadros voltados à comunidade, como "A Cidade Reclama", que ficou no ar até 2005, e o "Reage Bauru", exibido em 2002 nos telejornais da emissora.

A fase mais recente começou em 2003. A família do jornalista esportivo J. Hawilla comprou a TV Modelo e outras emissoras afiliadas da Globo em Sorocaba, São José do Rio Preto e Itapetininga, formando o grupo que hoje é a TV TEM .

Com a nova gestão, veio também a revolução tecnológica. A TV TEM liderou a transição para o sinal digital, em 2012, oferecendo imagem e som em alta definição muito antes de se tornar obrigatório.

J. Hawilla inaugurando o sinal digital da TV TEM em Bauru — Foto: Arquivo/TV TEM

"A ideia é estar sempre olhando para frente. O digital mudou o patamar da televisão", diz Stefano Hawilla, atual presidente da TV TEM.

"A gente busca sempre a identificação com o nosso público. O que eles vivem, o que querem ver, o que consomem nas cidades onde moram. Nosso papel é mostrar o interior do jeito que ele é, com sotaque, cultura, histórias reais e personagens que fazem a diferença", reforça Francine Ramagnoli, diretora de programação da TV TEM.

articles.title: ​An intruder breaks into a San Diego home, but Golden Retriever Nash keeps offering him toys; then police arrive, and the dog has the same plan, all caught on camera
articles.summary: US News: Dante Rowley and his fiancée were boarding a plane when the Ring camera alert arrived on their phone. A stranger was breaking into their home in Sherm.
articles.body: Dante Rowley and his fiancée were boarding a plane when the Ring camera alert arrived on their phone. A stranger was breaking into their home in Sherman Heights, climbing through a ladder to their second-story window near 20th and J streets. The Southern California couple watched it happen live through their security camera, helpless at 30,000 feet, as their worst nightmare started playing out on a screen.Then things got weird. Nash, their 4-year-old golden retriever, had one job that afternoon: sound the alarm and be the guard dog. But he had other plans. He treated the intruder like a long-lost friend, and the only thing the 90-pound golden dog wanted to do was play, ABC News reported.Intruder breaks in and gets cosyThe video shows an intruder hopping into the compound, then using a ladder to break into the second-story window. The man didn't exactly skulk around. He removed his shoes and shirt, settled onto a bench in the foyer, and raided the refrigerator for yoghurt, turkey and cheese. Then he took a nap. For roughly 30 minutes, he made himself completely at home.Then Nash showed up. The security footage shows Nash approaching the stranger, each time with a toy clenched in his mouth. The golden didn't even let out a warning bark. All the ‘guard dog’ did was offer toys and wag his tail. The intruder, to his credit, seemed bemused by the gesture. But Nash wasn't trying to be funny. He was genuinely convinced he'd met his new best friend.Then the cops showed upWhen police finally arrived, Nash's hospitality didn't waver. Officers found him at the door, tail wagging, toy still in his mouth, ready to extend the same warm welcome to anyone in uniform.The burglar, on the other hand, made a run for it. He attempted an escape through a bathroom window, only to find officers waiting in the backyard. He was arrested without much fuss.The suspect faced burglary charges, along with other outstanding warrants from unrelated incidents, according to NBC7. But Rowley surprised many with his response. Rather than dwell on the violation or anger, he expressed hope the man would get help. “We just hope he gets some help, honestly,” he told the outlet.Homeowner reactsNash wasn't alone when the stranger climbed through the window. One of the family's three dogs simply walked out through the doggy door and disappeared. Nash stayed put, apparently convinced he'd found his new best friend. The third wasn't home.Dante Rowley, the homeowner, wasn't mad at his furry babies for not confronting the intruder. “The dogs, we just wanted to make sure they were safe. Nash is not the greatest guard dog. We thought he was going to bark at people and he did the exact opposite,” Rowley told NBC7.Well, you see, this is not Nash's fault either. Golden retrievers aren't really known for their confrontation capabilities. They are great at retrieving game, swimming in cold water and living alongside humans in trusting harmony. Nash did exactly what his breed knows how to do. His actual calling was something different: bring joy to whoever walks through the door.So on that afternoon, when a stranger was raiding the refrigerator and a family was watching in real time from thousands of miles away, Nash did what he was supposed to do. He brought his toy, wagged his tail and made an intruder smile.In the end, didn't he do exactly what he was meant to do?Not just the intruder, Nash has brought a smile to the faces of millions of others, including you. The security footage hit social media, and people couldn't figure out how to feel. Was it terrifying or wholesome? Could it be both? The goofy golden's hospitality made many go ‘awww’. One netizen thought Nash was just protecting his precious toy. “He just wanted to make sure that toy wasn’t taken haha.” Others called him a good boy doing his best: “Well… if you didn’t already know he’s a good boy, now you know.” Nash didn't discriminate when it came to making new friends.As for Rowley, he acknowledged the obvious: Nash probably wouldn't be getting hired for security work anytime soon. But if the actual job was to make everyone feel genuinely welcome, the golden boy had already passed with flying colours.Perhaps that was Nash's job all along: to put a smile on everyone's face, even in the middle of a bizarre break-in. And be honest, are you smiling? Let us know in the comments below.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1830, Ohio flooded a swamp for a canal; one 50-acre bog rose with the water and became Buckeye Lake’s floating Cranberry Bog
articles.summary: US News: Explore the fascinating history and ecology of Buckeye Lake's floating Cranberry Bog, a natural wonder created by an engineering project in the 19th century.
articles.body: Construction of the Licking Summit Reservoir between 1826 and 1830 flooded a wetland known as Buffalo Lick, sometimes called the Great Swamp in local accounts, to create a water source for the Ohio and Erie Canal system. Most of the swamp disappeared under the rising water. One section did not. A roughly 50-acre mat of sphagnum moss, young and buoyant enough to tear free from the surrounding peat, rose with the water instead of sinking beneath it, detaching to form a floating island that has drifted on what became Buckeye Lake ever since.The 1826 to 1830 dike construction created Buckeye LakeConstruction of the dike started in 1826 and was completed by 1830. It was constructed to prevent the South Fork of the Licking River from flooding and to collect water for the canals. According to Ohio History Central, the reservoir was initially known as Licking Summit Reservoir, whereas the marshlands were historically known as Buffalo Lick as far back as the 1750s. It served as a landmark for Native Americans traveling from the Ohio River to Miami villages. As the Ohio Department of Natural Resources notes, the reservoir ultimately proved too shallow to reliably feed canal barge traffic during dry seasons, and the canal system itself fell out of use within a few decades. The reservoir was renamed Buckeye Lake by the Ohio State Legislature in 1894, as stated in the Licking Township Comprehensive Plan (Part 2), from which time it began to be used for recreation purposes, as the canal period came to a close.A section of bog mat rose with the water instead of sinkingWhat made this flood unusual wasn't the damage it caused, but what it left behind. In the swamp's northern reaches, a younger, more buoyant section of bog mat responded differently than the rest of the wetland: rather than submerging, it swelled like a water-saturated sponge, rose with the floodwaters, tore free from the surrounding peat, and became a true floating island.The bog earned National Natural Landmark status in October 1968The uniqueness of the floating bog has been officially acknowledged years after its discovery. The floating bog is one of the earliest National Natural Landmarks identified in Ohio, having been designated in October 1968, as stated in the list of National Natural Landmarks Designated 1967–1969 by the National Park Service, while the whole region was made a state nature preserve in 1977. According to the National Park Service, it is one of the few floating bog islands that are not connected to the land. Access to this fragile environment is restricted, though the Greater Buckeye Lake Historical Society organizes periodic tours, including a Cranberry Bog Day.Sphagnum moss and carnivorous plants define the preserveThis bog has had its ecosystem since the end of the ice age, as explained in the description of bogs by the National Park Service. This is because the plant life associated with this area, sphagnum mosses and the American cranberry, which lends its name to the bog, originated during the time after the Wisconsin Glacier retreated and boreal plant communities common to Canada established themselves here and have persisted in isolation despite climatic changes.In addition to this, the bog is home to carnivorous plants like round-leaved sundew and pitcher plants, as well as orchids that include pink calopogon, which flowers along with the cranberries every June. The water's acidity has historically sustained this plant community despite the warming climate surrounding it.The bog has shrunk from roughly 50 acres to an estimated 21 acres todayOver time, the floating bog has shrunk from its original roughly 50 acres, as measured by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources, to an estimated 21 acres today, with some estimates placing the actively floating portion at just 8 acres. It's worth noting the correlation between the bog's deterioration and shifting water chemistry in Buckeye Lake, where the acidity that once favored sphagnum moss and boreal plants has diminished over time. A similar acidity-driven decline has been documented at other bogs, such as Indiana's Pinhook Bog, according to the National Park Service. Nearly two centuries after an engineering effort meant to keep barges moving along central Ohio's canals, the accidental byproduct of that project, a piece of wetland adrift on rising water, has outlasted the canal system it was built for and become one of Ohio's most unique natural features.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2014, a Kentucky sinkhole opened beneath the National Corvette Museum before dawn and swallowed eight rare Corvettes from its Skydome exhibit
articles.summary: US News: In a dramatic turn of events, a sinkhole opened up beneath the National Corvette Museum in Kentucky, swallowing eight rare Corvettes, including prototypes and classic models, before dawn on February 12, 2014. Discover how this incident transformed into a permanent exhibit and a major attraction.
articles.body: On February 12, 2014, before daybreak, the floor of the Skydome exhibit hall in the National Corvette Museum in Bowling Green, Kentucky, collapsed, exposing a large sinkhole measuring 40 feet in width, 60 feet in length, and 30 feet in depth, according to the National Corvette Museum. Eight Corvettes on display fell into the hole along with slabs of concrete and display stands. Nobody got injured because it took place at about 5:38 a.m., before the museum had opened for its guests, as per the statement from the National Corvette Museum.The collapse struck before dawn on February 12, 2014Betty Hardison, the museum's security guard, was the first to learn of trouble at the Skydome when the alarm went off. Arriving at the scene, she found dust and smoke everywhere but no clear cause. Firefighters who responded soon after determined that part of the floor had collapsed, taking the eight cars down with it. According to the National Corvette Museum's own account of the event, the sinkhole's dimensions captured global attention almost immediately, and news crews and crowds gathered outside within hours.A collapsing limestone cave, not a structural failure, caused the holeConsequently, a later geological investigation discovered that the collapse resulted from the roof of a karst cave in the area under the Skydome that had slowly grown larger due to the erosive nature of the groundwater, according to Cars and Karst: Investigating the National Corvette Museum Sinkhole by Polk et al. (2015). It is because of this fact that when the roof of this limestone cave could no longer hold up the weight on top of it, it caved in.Eight cars, including a GM prototype, fell into the holeThe eight Corvettes that were victims of the sinkhole were spread across years of the car's existence. These cars included a 1962 Tuxedo Black Corvette, a 1984 PPG Pace Car, a 1992 One-Millionth Corvette, a 1993 40th Anniversary Corvette, a 1993 ZR-1 Spyder concept car, a 2001 Mallett Hammer Z06 donated by Kevin and Linda Helmintoller, and a 2009 ZR1 Blue Devil prototype on loan from General Motors. The car valuation company Hagerty valued the loss of all the vehicles at over $1 million.Recovery crews used cranes to lift the cars out over two monthsThe process of recovery commenced in March 2014 with cranes and workers being placed into the hole with the purpose of securing each car within a sling for removal back to the surface. The 2009 Blue Devil prototype, the 1962 Tuxedo Black Corvette, the 1984 PPG Pace Car, the 1993 40th Anniversary Corvette, and the 1992 One-Millionth Corvette were among those recovered in March 2014, according to the museum's official timeline. The rest of the cars were recovered in April 2014. The Blue Devil was in relatively good mechanical condition after being pulled from the hole, though it still required months of cosmetic and structural refurbishment by GM before its public unveiling, whereas some other cars needed far more extensive repair to become operational at all.Restoration took over a year for the most heavily damaged carsWhile some were restored quite fast, there were other cars that needed a lot of effort for the restoration. The Blue Devil was refurbished by GM and unveiled at the museum in February 2015, one year after the accident. The One Millionth Corvette took even longer, not returning to display until September 2015, after more than 1,200 hours of restoration work. Out of the eight cars that were found, five were not able to be fully restored because of heavy damage sustained during the fall.The site became a permanent exhibit rather than being erasedRather than erasing all trace of it, the museum's board opted to preserve part of the sinkhole's story as a permanent attraction. Much of the hole was filled in and floored over by mid-2015 for structural safety, leaving only an outlined footprint and a small viewing opening. The Corvette Cave-In exhibit, built around that footprint, opened in February 2016, exactly two years after the collapse, letting visitors see where the hole once was alongside the cars it damaged. Soil and stone samples taken from the sinkhole are sold in the gift shop of the museum at $10 per piece, and according to reports from the Associated Press and All That’s Interesting, thousands of pieces have been sold since the opening of the exhibition.From being a catastrophe for a specialized car museum in Bowling Green, the incident became one of its biggest draws. Over a decade later, the sinkhole continues to be a permanent fixture of the museum's collection, a reminder that even structures designed to house some of the rarest cars in American history can fall prey to the karstic formation in much of Kentucky's landscape.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Friday questioned student organisations, including the ABVP and NSUI, over alleged violations during the ongoing Delhi .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Friday questioned student organisations, including the ABVP and NSUI, over alleged violations during the ongoing Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) election process.The court asked: “Are you people students? You participate in meetings to ensure elections are held as per the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations, and then you do this?”The court was hearing a plea alleging violence and other violations during the DUSU election campaign. articles.title: A Finnish tunnel built for nuclear waste will be closed forever; its radioactive cargo must remain contained for 100,000 years
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Finland is building ONKALO, the world's first permanent geological repository for nuclear waste, designed to contain radioactive material for 100,000 years beneath Olkiluoto island.
articles.body: A repository is being prepared to permanently dispose of spent nuclear fuel more than 400 metres below the bedrock of Finland's Olkiluoto island. The facility is called ONKALO and is designed around multiple barriers that will isolate the radioactive material underground rather than keep it in an accessible storage building. Posiva, the Finnish company responsible for the project, says final disposal will take place at a depth of about 430 metres.The repository is being developed for spent nuclear fuel generated by Finland's nuclear power plants, and the fuel is first kept in interim storage while it cools. For final disposal, it will be encapsulated in metal canisters and placed inside deposition holes drilled into the bedrock. Bentonite clay will surround the canisters, while the tunnels will eventually be backfilled and sealed. Posiva lists the spent fuel, disposal canister, bentonite buffer, tunnel backfill and surrounding bedrock as parts of the system. The aim is to prevent radioactive material from reaching the surrounding environment over the long period in which the waste remains hazardous.The first real disposal hole is now being drilledPosiva began drilling the first deposition hole that is intended for actual final disposal more than 400 metres below the surface on August 26. The hole is being drilled vertically into the floor of a previously excavated final disposal tunnel, and when finished, it will be 8.4 metres deep and 1.75 metres in diameter. The drilling machine must maintain the hole within a maximum deviation of 25 millimetres from its vertical centre line along the full length. The machine itself weighs 78 tonnes, and Posiva says that drilling an eight-metre hole takes about 10 hours of effective drilling time under the site's conditions. The first holes are being checked particularly closely, and the first three will be measured again after completion before the project moves toward normal production.The first tunnel that is being worked on is about 330 metres long and is planned to contain roughly 30 deposition holes. Posiva does not plan to excavate the entire repository in advance; instead, new tunnels and deposition holes will be constructed as the disposal operation progresses. ONKALO began as a research and characterization facility that allowed engineers and geologists to study the Olkiluoto bedrock before the underground site became part of the final repository.The problem is measured in geological timeSpent nuclear fuel contains radioactive materials with very different decay times, and Posiva states that the penetrating gamma radiation from spent fuel disappears over a period of a few hundred years, but the fuel does not become comparable to natural uranium deposits until hundreds of thousands of years have passed. That is why ONKALO's safety concept extends far beyond the operating lifetime of an ordinary industrial facility. The repository is intended to remain sealed after the disposal operation is complete, and the surrounding rock and engineered barriers continue to isolate the material.The Science report supplied for this story describes the project as an attempt to create a permanent geological repository that is capable of containing nuclear waste over a period of around 100,000 years. The facility is being built inside ancient Finnish bedrock rather than relying on continued human maintenance at the surface.The project has also faced questions about how a repository can be assessed over periods far longer than recorded human history, since groundwater movement, corrosion, changes in the bedrock and future climate conditions all form part of the long-term safety problem.For now, ONKALO is still in the construction and commissioning stage rather than being a fully loaded permanent repository. The first deposition hole has only recently been drilled, and Posiva says the initial holes must pass detailed inspections before they can be approved for actual disposal. The current work therefore represents the transition from testing the underground system to preparing the holes that will eventually hold spent-fuel canisters. Once disposal is completed decades from now, the tunnels are intended to be backfilled and the repository closed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2008, a 20-foot hole opened in Daisetta, Texas; by the next day, it was a 900-foot, 260-foot-deep, water-filled crater that swallowed cars and oil tanks
articles.summary: US News: Explore the dramatic 2008 sinkhole in Daisetta, Texas, that transformed a small town into a geological spectacle as a massive crater developed overnight, swallowing cars and infrastructure.
articles.body: Located in Liberty County, Texas, about sixty miles northeast of Houston, Daisetta is a sleepy town with about a thousand residents. It has mostly been recognised, if at all, for perched above the Hull salt dome, a massive subterranean rock salt pillar that has attracted brine and oil drillers to the region since the early 1900s. The town's obscurity came to an abrupt end in the spring of 2008 when the ground beneath it collapsed, transforming a small pit into one of the biggest sinkholes ever discovered in the US. In just one day, what started out as a hole that was only twenty feet across grew into a churning crater that was hundreds of feet wide and deep enough to swallow telephone poles, cars, oil tanks and other equipment.A town built on a salt domeSalt domes like the one underneath Daisetta are formed when layers of heavy salt beneath progressively rise up over millions of years because they are lighter than surrounding rock. These domes are often near to the surface and trap pockets of oil and gas, which is why Liberty County has had drilling activities for decades. Sinkholes associated with salt domes can form when cavities develop within the cap rock or salt, and human activity can exacerbate or induce the process. For years the land above may look perfectly secure while the ground beneath is being silently hollowed away. According to the USGS, the ultimate Daisetta collapse was a textbook case of this process, with fluid poured into the dome. That slow underground erosion set the stage for what happened on the morning of 7 May 2008.The earth cracks openOn that Wednesday morning, residents saw a little sinkhole spring up along Farm to Market Road 770 on the edge of town. At first it seemed inconspicuous, little bigger than a swimming pool, and few people paid it much attention. But within hours the hole was expanding at an alarming rate and by the next day was a crater some 900 feet big and 260 feet deep. Local residents watched as the ground crumbled and swallowed up oil storage tanks, barrels, tyres, power poles and several vehicles. Witnesses said the sound was like a freight train going by. Emergency officials halted the nearby stretch of highway, evacuated buildings around the location and eventually had to alert curious sightseers who wanted a closer look at the widening pit. Around two days after the collapse, researchers from the University of Texas at Dallas quickly deployed a mobile laser scanning team to the site in the hope of capturing the changing shape of the crater before it stabilised.What led to its downfallThe Houston Geological Society placed the collapse on the northwest flank of the Hull salt dome, within a dense band of active and abandoned petroleum wells. Its 2008 bulletin noted at least four earlier sinkholes in the same band and said their occurrence, like that of the Daisetta collapse, might be related to oilfield operations that had begun in the early 1920s. The investigation highlighted that at least four other sinkholes had already occurred in the same region of active and abandoned wells, suggesting the 2008 occurrence was less a freak accident than the latest chapter in a trend related to decades of drilling. The Daisetta sinkhole is one of the largest ever documented along the salt domes of the Gulf Coast, averaging a diameter of around 620 feet. Fortunately no-one was killed or badly harmed, mostly because the fall was slow enough for bystanders to move away from the edges.A crater that remained part of DaisettaMore than a decade later, parts of the ground around the original crater crumbled again, a reminder that a salt dome filled with old wells rarely stops moving in one go and that a community founded on one has to live with that uncertainty forever. Today, the crater is partially filled with water and has become an unlikely local monument, visible from the highway, a lasting feature that still draws occasional curious visitors even as Daisetta has largely returned to normal. It is still a useful example for geologists to analyse how activities in an oilfield can speed up a natural process that might otherwise have taken centuries to reach the surface.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: From daily-wage labourer to entrepreneur: How Aajeevika Mission changed Sonbhadra woman’s life
articles.summary: How Aajeevika Mission Transformed Nirmala’s Life in SonbhadraIn the tribal and economically backward regions of Uttar Pradesh, a quiet transformation .
articles.body: How Aajeevika Mission Transformed Nirmala’s Life in SonbhadraIn the tribal and economically backward regions of Uttar Pradesh, a quiet transformation is taking place. Women who were once dependent on agricultural work and daily-wage labour for household survival are increasingly becoming entrepreneurs, managing businesses and contributing significantly to their families’ incomes.The story of Nirmala, a Scheduled Caste woman from Bichpai village in Robertsganj block of Sonbhadra district, is a compelling example of this change. Once dependent on daily wages, Nirmala of Bichpai village in Sonbhadra now earns around Rs 2.5 lakh annually. Her journey from labourer to entrepreneur reflects how the Aajeevika Mission is creating new opportunities for women in Uttar Pradesh’s rural and backward regions.Once compelled to work as a daily-wage labourer to support her six-member family, Nirmala has today established a diversified rural enterprise. Her annual income has risen to approximately Rs 2.5 lakh, while her success has inspired nearly 12 to 15 other women in her village to explore livelihood opportunities and move towards self-reliance.At the heart of this transformation is the Aajeevika Mission, being implemented by the Uttar Pradesh government to organize rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs), build their skills, facilitate access to financial assistance and encourage them to establish sustainable livelihood activities.Aajeevika Mission: From women’s groups to economic empowermentThe basic idea behind the Aajeevika Mission is to ensure that rural women are not merely recipients of welfare but become active participants in the rural economy.Through Self-Help Groups, women are brought together and encouraged to develop savings habits, acquire livelihood skills, access financial support and undertake income-generating activities. The SHG platform provides women with a collective support system that can help them overcome one of the biggest barriers faced by poor rural households—the lack of capital and access to organized livelihood opportunities. Nirmala’s journey demonstrates how this approach can translate into tangible economic empowerment.A graduate, Nirmala had the educational qualifications to aspire for a better future, but her family’s weak economic condition limited her opportunities. Her family consisted of her husband, three daughters and a son. Despite managing household responsibilities, she was forced to undertake wage labour to supplement the family income.Joining a Self-Help Group under the Aajeevika Mission became the first major turning point in her life. Instead of remaining dependent on irregular wage employment, Nirmala was introduced to skill development and livelihood opportunities. She received training in candle-making, a relatively low-investment activity with strong seasonal demand, particularly during festivals.She decided to convert this newly acquired skill into an enterprise. Seed capital turned s a skill into a business. Training alone cannot create a successful enterprise unless women also have access to the resources required to put their skills into practice. This is where financial assistance under the livelihood-development ecosystem became crucial for Nirmala.Recognizing her initiative, the Udyamita Vikas Pariyojana provided her with Rs 60,000 in seed money as initial assistance. For Nirmala, this support became the starting capital for her enterprise. She used the money to purchase moulds for making candles in different designs and shapes. Rather than limiting herself to conventional candles, she began producing attractive, colourful designer candles in the form of flowers, trees and other decorative figures.Initially, she focused on the festival market, particularly Deepawali, when demand for decorative candles rises sharply. What began as a seasonal activity gradually developed into a regular business as customers responded positively to her products. The transformation is significant: the woman who once sold her labour for daily wages was now producing a marketable product of her own.Diversification creates a stronger livelihoodNirmala’s journey also demonstrates another important principle of the Aajeevika Mission—livelihood diversification. Instead of depending on a single product, she gradually expanded her enterprise into different activities. With support from the Khadi Gramodyog Department, she received a popcorn-making machine, adding another source of income.She subsequently received specialized training from the Food Safety and Food Processing Department. The two-month training programme equipped her with skills to prepare value-added food products such as rose gulkand, sharbat and gajar ka murabba (carrot preserve).Nirmala now produces these products according to seasonal demand. This diversification has helped her move beyond a single festival-dependent enterprise towards a broader rural business model. Designer candles provide opportunities during the festive season, while food-processing products create additional avenues for income during other periods.In this way, different government interventions have complemented one another—SHG mobilization, skill development, seed capital, equipment support and food-processing training—to help convert a rural woman’s potential into a sustainable livelihood.Household responsibilities no longer stand in the wayNirmala’s success also challenges the traditional perception that women in rural areas can engage in economic activity only when they are relieved of household responsibilities. She continues to manage her family while simultaneously running her enterprise.This is one of the important social outcomes of the Aajeevika Mission. When livelihood activities are designed around the circumstances of rural women and are supported with training, finance and local opportunities, women can combine entrepreneurship with their responsibilities at home.The result is not merely an increase in income. It brings greater confidence, decision-making ability and social recognition. For Nirmala, entrepreneurship has given her an identity beyond that of a wage labourer.One woman’s success inspires an entire villageThe most powerful impact of Nirmala’s story can perhaps be seen in the women around her. Her success has encouraged 12 to 15 women in the village to move towards self-reliance. Her journey has demonstrated that entrepreneurship is possible even in a rural and economically disadvantaged area, provided women receive the right combination of training, institutional support and access to capital.This is precisely the larger objective of the Aajeevika Mission: creating an ecosystem in which one empowered woman can become a catalyst for change within her community. The transformation therefore extends beyond individual income. As more women join SHGs and take up enterprises, the economic role of women within rural households and communities becomes stronger.From self-reliance to market expansionNirmala is not stopping at her current achievements. Her next objective is to take her products to the online marketplace. This aspiration reflects the changing character of rural entrepreneurship in Uttar Pradesh.The journey that began with selling candles locally is now moving towards wider markets. Digital platforms can potentially help rural entrepreneurs overcome geographical limitations and connect their products with customers beyond their villages and districts. Nirmala’s ambition to enter the online market is therefore another important step—from local production to market expansion.A model of women-led rural developmentNirmala’s story illustrates the potential of a well-connected rural livelihood ecosystem.The Aajeevika Mission provided the institutional foundation by bringing her into the Self-Help Group network. Skill training gave her the capability to produce marketable goods. Seed money enabled her to purchase the equipment and raw materials necessary to begin production. Departmental support helped diversify her enterprise, while further training opened the door to food processing.The result is a woman who has moved from wage labour to entrepreneurship, from economic dependence to self-reliance and from individual struggle to becoming an inspiration for other women. Her journey also reflects the broader vision of the Yogi government to strengthen rural economies by empowering women as economic actors. In backward and tribal regions, where conventional employment opportunities can be limited, women-led micro-enterprises can provide an important alternative source of household income.Nirmala’s colourful candles may have been the first product of her enterprise, but they have come to symbolize something much larger—a new confidence among rural women. Today, Nirmala earns around Rs 2.5 lakh a year, manages her household and runs a diversified enterprise. More importantly, her story is encouraging other women in Bichpai to believe that self-reliance is possible.From a daily-wage worker to a rural entrepreneur, Nirmala’s journey is a powerful example of how Aajeevika Mission can transform skills into livelihoods, livelihoods into enterprises and individual success into a movement for women-led rural development.(District Transformation)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Gurgaon hit-and-run: Accused Kalyan Singh Bainsla, cousin Lavnish sent to 14-day judicial custody
articles.summary: GURGAON: A court on Friday sent hit-and-run accused Kalyan Singh Bainsla and his cousin Lavnish to 14 days' judicial custody, police said, days after .
articles.body: GURGAON: A court on Friday sent hit-and-run accused Kalyan Singh Bainsla and his cousin Lavnish to 14 days' judicial custody, police said, days after a video of the incident on Golf Course Road went viral.Earlier on Friday, a group of men were seen rallying in cars in support of Bainsla. A video showed several cars travelling together on a flyover in Haryana.Bainsla is accused of chasing and ramming the motorcycle of Gurgaon biker Sia, whose real name is Shivani Chauhan, on Golf Course Road on Sunday.Police said Bainsla had allegedly been returning from a club with his friends when the incident took place.Bainsla, Lavnish and other friends had gone to The Empire club at MGF Metropolitan Mall on MG Road on Saturday. Bainsla had borrowed a Maruti Ciaz from a friend for the outing. Police are yet to ascertain whether the accused were drunk.Police said Shrikant, an associate of Bainsla, was also in the car when the incident took place.According to sources, Lavnish allegedly instigated Bainsla to chase Chauhan and also allegedly abused her during the incident.Investigators said the accused followed Chauhan for around 2km. Bainsla allegedly asked her to stop. When she did not and instead signalled the car driver to move away, the accused allegedly rammed her motorcycle.A mahapanchayat was also called in support of Bainsla.Reacting to the support, Chauhan said the event was an attempt to “change the narrative” around the incident.“I don't understand this at all. Whatever is being done is just to change the narrative. It is not about the community, where they belong or the state. Something wrong happened to me on the road, and it can happen to anyone,” Sia said.She said the incident was not about gender or community.“It is not about a female or male rider. Anyone can lose their life. We are taking a stand so that such incidents can be prevented in the future. It hurts me when we divide wrongdoings on the basis of community,” she said.Sia said she did not know Bainsla's identity or background when the incident happened.“When this incident happened, I did not know his name, where he belonged or his caste. This is not about caste. All these things being done to change the narrative are illogical. articles.title: By 2019, Dave Matthews Band’s touring program had cut 121 million pounds of carbon pollution, avoided 478,000 plastic bottles and raised $2 million
articles.summary: US News: Discover how the Dave Matthews Band and REVERB transformed concert tours into a sustainability initiative, reducing carbon pollution, preventing plastic waste, and supporting environmental causes with $2 million raised.
articles.body: A concert tour leaves behind more than memories, merchandise and a packed venue. It also consumes fuel and electricity, generates food and packaging waste, and involves thousands of journeys by artists, crews and audiences. Dave Matthews Band began addressing those impacts in 2005, when it partnered with environmental organisation REVERB to bring sustainability into its touring operations. Over the following years, the initiative grew into a large-scale effort involving the band, its crew, venues, environmental groups and fans.According to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), by 2019 the partnership had eliminated 121 million pounds of carbon dioxide pollution, prevented 478,000 single-use plastic bottles from entering the waste stream and raised $2 million for environmental causes. These were cumulative figures covering 15 years of touring, 20 tours, 578 concerts and about 10 million fans, not figures from 2019 alone.Turning the tour itself into a sustainability projectIt began in 2005 with the band’s BamaGreen Project. REVERB partnered with the Dave Matthews Band to assess the environmental impact of its touring operations and make changes that could be applied consistently from one concert to the next. The idea behind it was straightforward, because the band toured through various cities; the environmental impact of that travel should be counted as part of the concert tour. Other changes were less straightforward. Tour buses used biodiesel fuel, while food provided on the tour was locally sourced. Backstage recycling and composting were also introduced, along with efforts to reduce disposable items. The team also calculated greenhouse gas emissions and funded offset projects.Bringing the audience into the effortThe environmental campaign was not confined backstage. Through the concert venues, REVERB managed the BamaGreen Eco-Village, where fans could connect with environmental organisations as well as learn about local initiatives. This made it possible for the environmental campaign to have a tangible presence at the concerts, as the audience did not just listen but also became participants.According to UNEP, fans took part in 731,000 eco-activities by 2019. The Eco-Village also hosted about 1,000 nonprofits that connected concertgoers with organisations working on environmental and sustainability issues. Plastic waste reduction was one of the programme’s most visible efforts. Water stations and reusable water bottles were used to avoid single-use plastics.The overall waste-management figures were also significant. According to the programme, 338,000 gallons of recyclables and 138,000 pounds of food waste were collected for composting. It also supported local agriculture through 2,100 family farms, and audiences and volunteers contributed about 24,500 hours of volunteer work. These figures show how small efforts at each concert can add up across hundreds of shows. A single refill station may have limited impact, but using them at every concert can save thousands of disposable bottles over a tour.From 2019 milestone to continuing programmeIt was not until 2019 that the scope of the effort drew recognition from the United Nations. That year, Dave Matthews Band was appointed a UNEP Goodwill Ambassador for using its influence to promote environmental initiatives. The tour programme did not end with that recognition. Instead, Dave Matthews Band continued its collaboration with REVERB on later tours, keeping measures such as refill stations, reusable bottles, recycling, composting and carbon accounting. In 2021, REVERB estimated that the tour avoided more than 28,000 single-use plastic bottles and tracked more than 41,000 fan activities through the Eco-Villages programme.The significance of the Dave Matthews Band effort is that the band built environmental work into its normal touring operations. By treating concerts as part of the full touring process, from transportation and catering to waste and fan engagement, the collaboration addressed all of those impacts. Thus, the 121 million pounds of carbon pollution and 478,000 bottles reported in 2019 reflected many years of similar actions. These numbers show what is possible when changes are built into a touring band’s infrastructure and carried from one concert to the next.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
